Q: using case statement to assign columnnames A:

This is what I meant

CASE WHEN PRIORITY='1' then  (ID)   END as 'BlockerIn',
CASE WHEN PRIORITY='2' then  (ID)  END  as 'CriticalOut'

This would create two columns with the values in.

If you want one column with multiple values you would do

CASE WHEN PRIORITY='1' then  'BlockerIn' 
WHEN PRIORITY='2' then  'CriticalOut' END  AS Priority

Q: Combine CASE expression with Inner Join for Alphanumeric OrderBY A:

You can separate both parts using a subquery:

SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT MCGroup, VisionMachinePerformance.MCSAP, ZAssetRegister.LocalName 
    FROM [VisionMachinePerformance]
    INNER JOIN ZAssetRegister ON VisionMachinePerformance.MCSAP=ZAssetRegister.SAP_Number
) DISTINCT_DATA
ORDER BY
    CASE WHEN PATINDEX('%[0-9]%',LocalName) > 1
         THEN LEFT(LocalName,PATINDEX('%[0-9]%',LocalName)-1) 
         ELSE LocalName END,
    CASE WHEN PATINDEX('%[0-9]%',LocalName) > 1
         THEN CAST(SUBSTRING(LocalName,PATINDEX('%[0-9]%',LocalName),LEN(LocalName)) as float)
         ELSE NULL END

Q: Snakemake workflow intermittently hangs on fastp after many hours, but fastp runs normally outside Snakemake A:

This doesn't really fit a Snakemake scheduling problem. Snakemake launches the process and waits for it to exit; if fastp is still present in the process table and sitting in SL+, there's not much for Snakemake to schedule at that point.

The fact that the affected sample changes every run is also significant. That argues against a corrupt FASTQ or some reproducible edge case in the input, since you'd expect the same file to trigger it consistently. Likewise, if the exact same fastp command completes normally when run outside the workflow, I'd be looking at whatever is different about the long-running pipeline environment rather than the command itself.

I'd inspect one of the hung processes before terminating it. A quick strace is often enough to tell whether it's repeatedly blocking on a futex, waiting on file I/O, or stuck somewhere else entirely. That would narrow things down a lot more than changing thread counts and hoping the behavior changes.

Q: How to hide includes from other classes? A:

There's fast pimpl idiom; it is much more ugly than pimpl but that is the most similar to using an opaque type by value (idea is for declaration to contain type-erased storage for the value instead of the value itself).

Others already mentioned modules - which would be similar Rust where InternalData definition is included but not available for user consumption.
